clinician.final_diagnosis: B-ALL associated with t(1;4) chromosomal abnormality
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 4-year-old Moroccan girl presented with a 20-day history of pharyngitis, progressive asthenia, pallor, and fever. Physical examination revealed a fistulated abscess in the left labia majora suggesting immunocompromise. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated pancytopenia with severe anemia (Hb 6.00 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (41,000 platelets), and neutropenia (570 neutrophils). Bone marrow aspiration revealed 97% blast cells with lymphoid morphology (heterogeneous size, reduced cytoplasm, condensed chromatin, basophilic cytoplasm without granulations) and absent megakaryocytes. Flow cytometry identified aberrant CD13 expression. Cytogenetic analysis demonstrated a clone with t(1;4)(p21;p15) in 10 of 20 mitoses, and FISH confirmed absence of MLL gene rearrangement. The patient completed 2 years of maintenance chemotherapy from November 2016 to September 2019 and achieved complete remission, remaining disease-free at age 11.
